submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective detector for verb forms of the lemmas DO, SKIP and BREAK when they describe carrying out, omitting, or interrupting an expected action or routine; it peaks on the verb token itself and fires more strongly when a negation, refusal or non-completion marker (not, n't, refusing, declined, fear of not) appears nearby. Near-synonyms outside these lemmas (eat, smash, complete, read) in identical frames do not drive it, and the sense within a lemma (violating probation versus breaking glass) does not matter.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the audit, the board asked why the finance team chose not to do more to flag suspicious payments, and the report demanded tighter oversight of transfers.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel business context with bare ' do' and a nearby negation ('not'), the negation-plus-DO-form configuration the hypothesis says fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She did the whole assignment in a single night, then slept through the weekend and missed the tutorial that her tutor had scheduled for Monday morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New school context for ' did' as a DO form denoting carrying out an expected task; the hypothesis predicts firing, only less strongly than with a negation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The coach does the warm-up with the entire squad himself, so nobody on the team can later claim that the drills were never explained or demonstrated.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sports holdout for ' does', a claimed present-tense DO form that none of the top examples shows.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Either party may end this agreement without doing harm to any rights already accrued, provided written notice of termination is served thirty days in advance.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Legal-register holdout for ' doing' in the sense of causing harm; the hypothesis's clause that sense within a lemma does not matter predicts it fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: By the time the safety inspector arrived, the crew had already done the repairs, cleared the site and loaded the scaffolding back onto the lorry.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Completion frame in a maintenance setting for ' done', a claimed form absent from all the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: # Build step: skip the cache warm-up whenever the runner is offline, otherwise the job fails on the first network request and the pipeline stalls.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre code-comment holdout with imperative ' skip' for omitting an expected build step.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He refused to practise the scales and kept skipping the lessons, so his piano teacher rang home to ask whether anything had happened at school.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New context for ' skipping' with a nearby refusal marker ('refused'), which the hypothesis says is the strongest configuration.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Nurses who break the sterile procedure must report the lapse at once, and the ward reviews every such case at its weekly team meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Rule-violation sense of ' break' in a hospital setting, testing the claim that the sense within a lemma does not matter.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The fire alarm sounded at seven, breaking the morning quiet and sending everyone in the office down the stairs and out into the car park.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Interruption-of-routine holdout with ' breaking' in a novel office scene, the lemma's core claimed meaning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The striker broke the club record for goals in a season, and the fans sang his name for the rest of the evening at the ground.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Idiomatic ' break a record' sense of ' broke'; the hypothesis's sense-invariance clause predicts firing even with no routine being interrupted.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The result was a major time savings, largely the result of not reading every draft report in full before the weekly editorial budget meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Exact frame of example 3 with the trigger replaced by a named near-synonym ('reading'), which the hypothesis says does not drive the unit.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We set predictable consequences for our son: timeouts, taking away toys, forgoing story time, early bedtimes, but never physical punishment or long solitary timeouts.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 4's discipline frame with 'forgoing' in place of 'skipping'; a non-lemma synonym in the same position, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: But then in March he was arrested for petitioning to revoke the arrangement, which means violating probation, and a judge ordered a new hearing in April.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 1's probation frame with 'violating' replacing 'breaking'; identical concept, non-lemma word, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rash is often linked to treatment with fluorouracil, capecitabine and liposomal daunorubicin, and usually presents as tingling and soreness in the hands and feet.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 8's chemotherapy frame with a drug name that has no ' do' subword, so no claimed DO token appears anywhere.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The latest headlines in your inbox twice a day, Monday to Friday, plus evening news updates. Enter your email address below to continue reading.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 7's newsletter template with 'breaking' removed; same topic and layout, no claimed BREAK token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Momentum compounds in the market as investors buy near the top for fear of not performing as well as or better than their peers.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 2's investing frame with 'performing' replacing 'doing'; negation plus near-synonym but no DO token, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After initially refusing to comply with the order, the club was fined and warned that any further delay would trigger a points deduction this season.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After two hours of stacking shelves, the crew took a short break in the back room and shared a bag of crisps and a flask of tea.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' break' occurs only as a noun ('a short break'), not a verb form, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: His big break came when a scout saw him play in a minor league match and offered him a professional contract that same summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Nominal 'big break' gives the surface token without the claimed verb form; a trigger token in a wrong context, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The builders filled the skip outside the house with rubble, cracked tiles and old lead pipes, then ordered another one for the following week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' skip' occurs only as a noun for a waste container, not as a verb of omission, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Three does grazed at the edge of the wood while the stag watched from the treeline and the walkers kept very still behind the gate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' does' here is the plural of 'doe', not a form of the lemma DO, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Regulators opened a fresh inquiry into the failed drug trial and asked the sponsor to hand over every trial record from January onwards without delay.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same regulatory topic as example 8 but with no DO/SKIP/BREAK token anywhere; a same-topic, no-feature control.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The school's behaviour policy lists detentions, letters home and the loss of playtime privileges, but it rules out any form of physical punishment entirely.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The consequences-of-misbehaviour topic of example 4 with none of the claimed lemma tokens present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Investors who chase momentum near market tops often buy at the worst possible moment, and the compounding effect can be brutal in a downturn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 2's market-momentum topic stripped of any DO form, testing that topic alone does not drive the unit.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The whole theatre team follows a fixed checklist before every operation, and the anaesthetist signs it off at the end of the printed list.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Routine-procedure topic with no claimed lemma token; same topic, no feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Goggles, gloves, apron, closed shoes and tied hair are required at the bench, and food or drink is not permitted anywhere in the laboratory.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Comma-delimited list carrying the punctuation that sits next to the examples' peaks but no DO/SKIP/BREAK form, so neither delimiter nor topic should fire it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clinic switched him from doxycycline to a cheaper antibiotic after the infection had cleared and his blood counts returned to normal that spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A ' do'-initial drug name in the same chemotherapy frame; the hypothesis restricts itself to verb forms, so a subword ' do' in a drug name is predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She completed her morning routine in complete silence, made the bed, started the coffee and was out of the door before anyone else woke.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A named near-synonym ('completed') in the do-the-routine sense, which the hypothesis says does not drive the unit.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The coach told the whole squad to abandon the warm-up and go straight into the match, since the rain had finally stopped by then.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase of omitting an expected action using the non-lemma verb 'abandon', predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dietitian told him to eat fried food only on Sundays and to start each morning with fruit and porridge instead of the usual pastries.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The named near-synonym 'eat' in a routine/diet frame like the examples' omission contexts, predicted inactive.
